lines: Seventeen across: 'small kindness, nine letters.' I'm going to say it's you, kid.
Ha — my pen! Knew I left it up at the pond.
Next time you're at the counter, tell Hannah your coffee's on me.

effects.toast: Episode complete — new story next week

lines: Take Route 10 north to Jefferson. There's a bench by the mill pond, near the inn. That's my puzzle spot.
'Morning. You're the new one, right? Up past the town hall in Jefferson?
I was up there Wednesday for pizza night at the Mill Pond — and somewhere between the pond and here I lost my crossword pen.
Forty years of Saturday puzzles with that pen. If you're headed back north, would you look by the bench?
Earl showed everybody the pen. Twice. You're famous now.
Is that Earl's pen? Oh, he's going to be insufferable about the puzzle this week.
Go on — he's right out front.
Morning! Coffee's on, and yes, the make-your-own sundae bar is real.
If you're looking for Earl, he holds court out front most mornings.
A fine ballpoint, half-buried in the grass by the pond bench. This has to be Earl's.
Chalkboard by the tavern door: pizza night Monday and Wednesday. A second line, underlined twice: RIBS SOLD OUT.
Posted hours end at 2 PM most days. The board agenda lists road salt bids and 'the goat situation (continued).'
A hand-lettered sign: PRIME RIB SATURDAY — MAKE A RESERVATION. WE MEAN IT.
Someone inside is laughing at the bar.
A customer is explaining, with great intensity, that the chocolate chip cookie is somehow vegan.
The menu board offers a mac-n-cheese burger, and it is not a dare.
A dog outside is finishing a pup cup with real focus.
Someone orders a Maple Smoke latte — maple, a pinch of liquid smoke, sea salt.
Through the side doorway, the Catskill Outpost shelves are calling.
Bat signs point around back to the patio. Tonight's board: tacos, then a movie.
It sounds like everybody in there knows everybody.
A taped-up flyer teases a big-name comedian, headed this way one of these days — DATE TBA. Guess you'll just have to keep checking back.
Shelves of the essentials: chips, motor oil, birthday candles, one lonely jigsaw puzzle.
The ice cream case hums along beside them. Taped to the glass, a hand-written sheet keeps the softball league standings current.
Through the window, the owner is walking a couple through an Austrian orange wine. Nobody leaves this shop empty-handed.
